v.why: Replacing a parameter-free pooling on the final edge with a 3x3 conv gives large gains on all datasets.
Swapping avg_pool for a conv on edge 5 consistently improves accuracy.
Replacing pooling on the input edge with a conv yields large gains, up to about +10 points.
Replacing pooling on edge 1 with a 3x3 conv is positive on all datasets in most cases.
With edge 4 absent, removing edge 3 cuts a main path into the output, causing a very large drop.
With only a weak skip on edge 3, removing edge 5 leaves the output starved of learned features, causing a large drop.
Replacing a 3x3 conv on the input edge with a skip loses capacity.

raw:
I took these from the 100 measurements plus how the cell's paths work. Most of the data comes from a single condition per edit, so those hypotheses rest on direction and size of the effect rather than a direct contrast with other parents.

1. Replacing an avg_pool_3x3 on edge 5 with a conv gains a lot. This holds for both nor_conv_3x3 (+1 to +7 points) and nor_conv_1x1 (+0.5 to +6).
2. Setting edge 0 to nor_conv_1x1 gains most when it replaces avg_pool_3x3 (up to about +10 points).
3. Setting edge 1 to nor_conv_3x3 gains when it replaces avg_pool_3x3 (positive on all three datasets in most cases).
4. Removing edge 3 hurts much more when edge 4 is none, because it cuts the main path into the output (-11 on ImageNet16-120, against about -1 with a skip on edge 4).
5. Removing edge 5 hurts a lot when edge 3 is skip_connect, because the output then depends heavily on edge 5 (-5 to -14 on ImageNet16-120).
6. Replacing nor_conv_3x3 on edge 0 with skip_connect loses accuracy (mostly negative across datasets).
7. Removing a nor_conv_3x3 on edge 1 loses accuracy (consistently negative).
8. Replacing nor_conv_3x3 on edge 5 with skip_connect loses accuracy, mostly on C100 and ImageNet16-120.
9. Replacing nor_conv_3x3 on edge 2 with skip_connect loses accuracy (mostly negative).

The JSON also lists a tenth hypothesis (edge 4 to skip_connect when edge 4 is avg_pool_3x3). It rests on small positive changes, mostly on ImageNet16-120, so it is the weakest.
